+

+  res.exc := fma.io.exceptionFlags

+//******************************************************************************
+// Area- and timing-tuned replacement for rocket's PipelinedMultiplier.
+//******************************************************************************
+
+package boom.v3.exu
+
+import chisel3._
+import chisel3.util._
+
+import freechips.rocketchip.rocket.{MultiplierReq, MultiplierResp}
+
+/**
+ * Drop-in replacement for freechips.rocketchip.rocket.PipelinedMultiplier.
+ *
+ * Same IO, same fixed latency, bit-identical results -- but the 64x64 product is
+ * built from four unsigned 32x32 products spread over two pipeline stages instead
+ * of one monolithic combinational multiply.
+ *
+ * Why, part 1 (frequency).  Rocket registers the request, then computes the whole
+ * product *and* the result mux in a single cycle, and follows it with
+ * (latency-1) = 2 registers that do nothing but delay.  In this tile that one
+ * combinational block owns the five worst paths in the entire design (19.10ns of
+ * a 20ns period); the next endpoint family anywhere, core -> rename busytable,
+ * finishes in 18.55ns.  Splitting the multiply across the registers that were
+ * already being paid for costs no latency and hands the period back.
+ *
+ * Why, part 2 (area).  Chisel's `lhs * rhs` on two 65-bit SInts is lowered by
+ * firtool to an *unsigned* 128x128 multiply with both operands explicitly
+ * sign-extended ({{64{sign}}, in} * {{64{sign}}, in}); Yosys then builds a
+ * partial-product array for those declared widths.  Clipped to the 128 bits that
+ * are used that is sum(128-j, j=0..127) = 8256 PP bits.  The decomposition below
+ * needs 4 x 32 x 32 = 4096 -- half -- because every product is genuinely
+ * unsigned and exactly 32 bits wide, and the sign of the operands is handled by a
+ * single correction term instead of by 63 replicated bits per operand.
+ *
+ * The algebra, with a1/a0 and b1/b0 the high/low halves of the two operands and
+ * sa/sb the (masked) sign bits:
+ *
+ *   lhs = in1 - sa*2^64 , rhs = in2 - sb*2^64
+ *   lhs*rhs = in1*in2 - (sa*in2 + sb*in1)*2^64 + sa*sb*2^128
+ *
+ * Only 128 bits of the product are ever read, so the sa*sb*2^128 term vanishes
+ * and the correction is a plain 64-bit value applied at bit 64:
+ *
+ *   prod[127:0] = a0*b0 + (a1*b0 + a0*b1)<<32 + (a1*b1 - corr)<<64   (mod 2^128)
+ *
+ * corr is built straight from the s0 operands, so it is off the multiplier's
+ * critical path and is folded into a1*b1's register.  prod[31:0] is a0*b0[31:0]
+ * verbatim, so stage 2 only has to add the top 96 bits.
+ */
+class BoomPipelinedMultiplier(width: Int, latency: Int, nXpr: Int = 32) extends Module
+{
+  require(width % 2 == 0)
+  require(latency >= 3)
+
+  val io = IO(new Bundle {
+    val req  = Flipped(Valid(new MultiplierReq(width, log2Ceil(nXpr))))
+    val resp = Valid(new MultiplierResp(width, log2Ceil(nXpr)))
+  })
+
+  val hw = width / 2
+
+  // ---- s0: the input register rocket has, unchanged -----------------------
+  val in = Pipe(io.req)
+
+  // Exactly the three control bits rocket's DecodeLogic minimises to over
+  // {FN_MUL=0, FN_MULH=1, FN_MULHSU=2, FN_MULHU=3}:
+  //   cmdHi = fn[0]|fn[1], lhsSigned = !(fn[1]&fn[0]), rhsSigned = !fn[1]
+  val cmdHi     =   in.bits.fn(0) || in.bits.fn(1)
+  val lhsSigned = !(in.bits.fn(1) && in.bits.fn(0))
+  val rhsSigned = !(in.bits.fn(1))
+  val cmdHalf   = (width > 32).B && in.bits.dw === 0.U  // DW_32 === false.B
+
+  val a1 = in.bits.in1(width-1, hw)
+  val a0 = in.bits.in1(hw-1, 0)
+  val b1 = in.bits.in2(width-1, hw)
+  val b0 = in.bits.in2(hw-1, 0)
+  val sa = lhsSigned && in.bits.in1(width-1)
+  val sb = rhsSigned && in.bits.in2(width-1)
+
